long_biography.plain_text:
Limited telephone infrastructure made much of Africa a difficult market when Mo Ibrahim established Celtel in 1998. He approached the problem as an engineer, drawing on doctoral research in mobile communications and experience at British Telecom. Celtel used regional networks and prepaid service to reach customers poorly served by fixed lines, expanding across numerous African markets.

The sale of Celtel in 2005 gave Ibrahim the resources for a second institution-building phase. He created the Mo Ibrahim Foundation to measure governance, convene public debate and recognise African leaders who leave office with strong records. Alongside that public work, he founded Satya Capital to invest in African businesses. Ibrahim remains founder and chair of the foundation and founding chairman of Satya.
